messages:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change I'm seeing ~12% higher p99 for long-seq chat workloads when KV cache is sharded across TP. Profiling attached.

perf-bot: Alert: perf-regression detected for job redwood-chat-pt at 2026-03-18T08:12:34Z (p99 +12%). Trace id: trc_83b2.

ajay: Did you compare TP-sharded KV vs PP-local KV? IIRC kernel-selector swapped to cheaper elementwise kernels which may increase small-allreduce frequency. :thinking:

maria: Quick paste from the nvtx timeline (trimmed):
```
step 42 timeline:
  compute (attention kernels): 58ms
  all_reduce (kv index sync): 36ms blocking
  kv-lookup kernel: 4ms
  launch overheads (many small nccl calls): ~15ms total
```
Not huge compute change, but the all_reduce stalls are back-to-back and don't overlap with next compute.

kevin: That looks like communication fragmentation. When KV is sliced per TP shard we spawn one small all-reduce per shard per microbatch. Kernel selector change probably reduced fusion so fewer contiguous reductions to coalesce.

rachel: Can we try 2 quick toggles: 1) force fused allreduce path, 2) switch kv.shard_strategy=pp (keep KV local to PP stages) to see delta. Command I used previously:
```
./run_profile --model=redwood-7b --tp=2 --pp=2 --kv-shard=tp --kernel-selector=default --trace nvtx
```
Change to `--kv-shard=pp` and `--kernel-selector=fused-nccl` for the test.

ajay: Also capture `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` or nvtx markers; we need to confirm kernel launch density vs raw bandwidth usage. If the all-reduce calls are many small ops NCCL overhead dominates.

maria: Good call. One weird bit: DP fallback (single replica with dp across microbatches) had lower p99 in our runs. Likely because DP aggregates reductions across the whole replica and amortizes comm cost.

kevin: Yup — DP effectively reduces the number of tiny reductions. For TP+PP we should consider:
- coalescing KV indices per step (aggregate KV syncs into batched all-reduce), or
- increase microbatch size so fewer syncs, or
- route small KV updates through an async pipeline to overlap with compute.

rachel: For immediate experiment: toggle `runtime.coalesce_kv_syncs=true` (dev flag) and flip `kernel_selector.mode=throughput`. That should let NCCL fuse ops.

maria: I'll run three experiments (baseline, fused-allreduce, coalesce_kv_syncs) on the same input set and post end-to-end p50/p99 + nvtx traces. ETA ~2h. :thumbsup:

ajay: Thanks — once you post traces I can run a quick script to measure average all-reduce size and frequency. If mean message < 256KB we need fusion.

perf-bot: perf-note: experiment jobs started: exp_181900_a (fused), exp_181900_b (coalesce), exp_181900_c (kv->pp). Links: https://ci/reports/exp_181900_a

kevin: If experiments show coalescing helps, we should consider a synthesis where kernel-selector picks fused kernels only when kv_shard=tp and mean_kv_msg_size < X. Otherwise fallback to cheaper kernels.

maria: Agreed. Also we might add a perf regression check that flags p99 delta when kv_shard=tp after kernel-selector changes so we don't ship blind.

rachel: Nice. If you need a quick patch for coalesce flag I can whip one up and deploy to the canary pool.

maria: Please do. I'll upload nvtx traces to the report when done.

perf-bot: note: trace uploads complete for exp_181900_a at 1819005256.

ajay: Great — I'll start parsing now.

maria: Thanks team. Will post numbers soon.
